title: "Reference"
subtitle: "Every name Lanterne exports, and what it accepts."
description: "The five exports of lib.typ, the theme token vocabulary, the slide options, and what each call rejects."
---

`lib.typ` is a pure re-export facade: it exports five names and defines none.
Everything below was read out of the source, and each section names the file it came from, so it can be checked against the code rather than trusted.

| Export | Source | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `deck` | `src/render/deck.typ` | The document's show rule: a body becomes pages. |
| `slide` | `src/core/slides.typ` | A slide written out in full rather than opened by a heading. |
| `slide-options` | `src/core/slides.typ` | Options for the slide a heading opened. |
| `theme-tokens` | `src/theme/theme.typ` | A theme: the defaults with named overrides applied. |
| `theme-merge` | `src/theme/theme.typ` | Overrides merged into a complete theme. |

: The public surface. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[20,30,50]"}

Anything a module exports that is not listed here is internal on purpose.
`register-container` is the notable absence: it builds a container registry, and the only function that reads one is internal, so exporting it would hand out a value with nowhere to put it.
It arrives with the deck option that takes a registry.

## `deck`

Read from `src/render/deck.typ`.

```typst
#show: deck.with(theme: theme-tokens(), aspect-ratio: "16-9", slide-level: 2)
```

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `body` | content | | The document, passed by the show rule. |
| `theme` | dictionary or `none` | `none` | A token dictionary from `theme-tokens` or `theme-merge`. `none` takes the canonical defaults. |
| `aspect-ratio` | `"16-9"` or `"4-3"` | `"16-9"` | The page shape. |
| `slide-level` | non-negative integer | `2` | The heading level that opens a slide. `0` disables heading splitting. |
| `info` | dictionary | `(:)` | Document metadata, passed to `set document`. |

: `deck` arguments. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[15,18,12,55]"}

`aspect-ratio` selects one of Typst's own presentation papers: `"16-9"` is 841.89pt by 473.56pt, and `"4-3"` is 793.7pt by 595.28pt.

### `info` keys

| Key | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | content or string | The document title. |
| `author` | string or array of strings | One author or several. |
| `date` | datetime, `auto` or `none` | The document date. |

: `info` keys, the three `set document` reads. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[15,30,55]"}

The vocabulary carries only what something reads.
Typst's own `description` and `keywords` are not among them, and an unknown key is rejected rather than passed through.

### How a body becomes slides

One pass over the body's top level children, splitting at anything that opens a slide.

| Boundary | Opens |
| --- | --- |
| A heading at `slide-level` | A content slide, titled by that heading. |
| A heading below `slide-level` | A section slide, whose content is centred on the page. |
| A heading above `slide-level` | Nothing: it is ordinary content on the slide it sits in. |
| `#pagebreak()` | An untitled slide, even when nothing follows it. |
| `slide(...)` | A slide complete in itself; what follows opens another. |

: What opens a slide. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[40,60]"}

Content before the first boundary is an implicit untitled slide, and is dropped when nothing in it puts a mark on the page.

Only top level children are examined, so a heading nested inside a block, a grid cell or a list item never splits the deck.
The same limit applies to `slide-options`, which has to be a top level child of the slide it configures.

A heading that opens a slide stays where it was written, at the head of that slide's body, rather than being lifted out and re-emitted.
That is what keeps `set heading(numbering: ...)`, a `show heading` rule and a reference to a labelled heading all working on it.

::: {.callout-note}

## A `set heading(offset: ...)` rule is invisible to the split

A heading's level is read from the heading itself, under whichever of `level`, `depth` and `offset` the author reached for.
An offset set by a rule lives in the style wrapper, and Typst exposes no way to read a wrapper's rules, so such a heading splits at the level it was written at rather than the level it renders at.
Write the level you mean, or set `slide-level` to match the offset.
An `offset` passed to `heading` itself is a field, so it is read and counted.
:::

## `slide`

Read from `src/core/slides.typ`.

```typst
#slide(title: [A slide of one's own])[
  An explicit slide is complete in itself.
]
```

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `body` | content | | The slide's content, as the one positional argument. |
| `title` | content or `none` | `none` | The slide's title. |
| `level` | positive integer or `none` | `none` | The heading level the title stands at. Defaults to the deck's `slide-level` when a title is given. |
| `..attrs` | named only | | Slide options, validated as for `slide-options`. |

: `slide` arguments. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[15,20,12,53]"}

A second positional argument is rejected, as is a `slide-options` call inside the body: an explicit slide's options are its own arguments, so write `slide(smaller: true)[...]`.

## `slide-options`

Read from `src/core/slides.typ`.

```typst
== Set smaller

#slide-options(smaller: true)
```

Named arguments only.
The call is a marker the splitter consumes and never renders, and it must be written immediately after the slide's heading: nothing but the heading and blank content may precede it.
Two markers on one slide are an error rather than one of them silently winning.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `smaller` | boolean | `false` | Sets the slide's text one step down the theme's `scale-ratio`, title and body together. |

: Slide options, from `src/core/record.typ`. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[15,13,12,60]"}

One option today.
`steps`, `appendix` and `layout` arrive alongside the code that reads them, so the vocabulary grows rather than shipping names that mean nothing yet.

## `theme-tokens` and `theme-merge`

Read from `src/theme/theme.typ`.

```typst
#let base = theme-tokens(bg: rgb("#fbfbfd"), fg: rgb("#1c1c22"))
#let dark = theme-merge(base, (bg: rgb("#1c1c22"), fg: white))
```

`theme-tokens(..overrides)` takes named arguments only and returns the canonical defaults with those overrides applied.
`theme-merge(base, overrides)` takes a complete token dictionary and a dictionary of overrides, and validates every key of both.

`base` must be complete rather than a subset.
A partial one would flow downstream and fail where it is read, naming a missing key, rather than here, naming the theme that lacks it.

`extra` merges key by key rather than replacing wholesale, so setting one token of your own leaves the base theme's others in place.

### Token vocabulary

Read from `src/theme/tokens.typ`.
The colour, typography and geometry groupings are documentation rather than structure: the dictionary is flat, so a theme merges without recursion and a generated theme is one dictionary literal.

| Token | Accepts | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bg` | colour | `white` | The page fill. |
| `fg` | colour | `rgb("#111111")` | The text colour. |
| `dim-opacity` | ratio from 0% to 100% | `30%` | Reserved for dimmed content behind an overlay step. Validated, and read by nothing until the step engine lands. |
| `font-base` | family name, coverage-scoped entry, or a non-empty array of them | `"Libertinus Serif"` | The body font. |
| `font-heading` | as `font-base` | `"Libertinus Serif"` | The heading font. |
| `size-base` | positive absolute length | `24pt` | The body text size. An `em` value is rejected here, since it would be relative to itself. |
| `scale-ratio` | number of at least 1 | `1.2` | The step between heading sizes, and what `smaller` divides by. |
| `weight-heading` | integer from 100 to 900, or a weight name | `"semibold"` | The heading weight. |
| `leading` | length | `0.75em` | The paragraph leading. |
| `margin` | length | `2cm` | The page margin. |
| `extra` | dictionary | `(:)` | Tokens of your own. The one key whose contents are not validated. |

: The token vocabulary. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[15,25,15,45]"}

The named weights are `thin`, `extralight`, `light`, `regular`, `medium`, `semibold`, `bold`, `extrabold` and `black`.

A heading's size is `size-base` multiplied by `scale-ratio` raised to `max(0, 3 - level)`, so a section title reads as larger than a slide title and both read as larger than the body, and level 3 and below sit at the base size.
On a slide set `smaller`, the base of that calculation is the slide's own reduced size, so the title shrinks with the body rather than staying as large on the slide that asked for room.

`extra` exists so that a token of your own has somewhere to live.
The strictness everywhere else is the point: a mistyped token name that is quietly ignored is how a theme rots.
`extra` is not itself a token name, so `theme-tokens(extra: ...)` is accepted as a key while `check-token` reports `extra` as an unknown token name.

## The slide record

Read from `src/core/record.typ`.
A record is the one dictionary a slide is described by, and is what the renderer reads.
It is not exported, and is documented here because it is the contract the machine surface will be built on.

| Key | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `"content"` or `"section"` | A section slide is a divider, and must have a title. |
| `title` | content or `none` | The heading's body, describing the slide. |
| `level` | positive integer or `none` | The level that heading stands at. |
| `label` | label or `none` | The heading's label, carried because content equality ignores labels. |
| `attrs` | dictionary | Every slide option, each unnamed one at its default. |
| `body` | content | What renders, the opening heading included. |

: The slide record. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[12,25,63]"}

`title` and `level` stand or fall together: a title with no level describes a heading at no level, and a level with no title describes a heading that is not there.

There is no `layout` key.
Layouts arrive with the code that resolves them, and a key nothing reads is a key whose meaning no reader can check.

## Validation

Every validation in the package routes through `src/utils/errors.typ`, so every message has the same grammar:

```text
<scope>: <problem>; got <repr(value)>. <hint>
```

`<scope>` is the function the author called, not the helper that raised the error: a token rejected on behalf of `theme-tokens` names `theme-tokens`.
Typst cannot catch a panic, so every one of these is a compile error rather than something a deck can recover from.

Three shapes cover the failures:

Enumerated values

: `deck: aspect-ratio must be one of "16-9", "4-3"; got "21-9".`

Types and shapes

: `theme-tokens: bg must be a colour; got 1.`

Everything else

: `slide-options must come before the slide's content. Move the slide-options call to just after the heading.`

`tests/expect-fail/` is the authoritative list of what each guard rejects: one file per case, each carrying the exact message it must produce.
A guard cannot be exercised from inside a unit test, because Typst cannot catch a panic, so those cases compile files that are asserted to fail.

## Limitations

What is specified but not implemented, as of the current development state:

Overlay steps

: `#pause` and the step functions do not exist, so a slide renders as one page. `dim-opacity` and the `steps` slide option are part of the same milestone.

Layouts and chrome

: A slide is its title and its body. There is no header, footer, progress indicator, slide number or logo, and no layout system to place them.

The element catalogue

: Callouts, columns and the rest of the structural elements are not implemented.

Reconstruction of unknown elements

: The traversal refuses, loudly, to rebuild an element it has no registry entry for, rather than guessing. A deck that silently lost a step boundary is worse than one that failed to build. `notes/roundtrip-findings.md` records which elements were characterised and how.

Markers inside `context`

: A marker inside a `context` block is invisible to the traversal, because a context block reports no fields until layout resolves it. Anything the traversal must see has to be written outside `context`.

Cross references by name

: A labelled heading is a link destination, so `#link(<label>)` works. Typst refuses `@label` on a heading that is not numbered, so referencing by name waits for the numbering rules.
